choice: Represent direct N2/H2 ammonia synthesis by dissociative adsorption/hydrogenation on Fe, Co, and conventional Ru, while allowing promoted Ru/electride/hydride catalysts to shift the rate-controlling step from N2 cleavage to N-H formation; use a common reversible overall reaction thermodynamic constraint rather than forcing one elementary RDS on every catalyst.
alternatives: Universal N2-dissociation-limited mechanism for every catalyst
Associative N2 hydrogenation mechanism for every catalyst
Separate bespoke elementary mechanism fitted independently to each paper
reason: The catalyst set spans Fe, Co, Ru, electrides, hydrides, imides, and MXene-like supports; the literature explicitly reports an RDS shift for Ru/C12A7:e−, so a universal irreversible RDS would mis-transfer activity, while paper-level data are insufficient to fit bespoke mechanisms.

choice: Use each record's measured NH3 productivity as the local forward-capacity anchor at its reported T and P, and convert it to plant net productivity with a reversible approach-to-equilibrium factor (1-Q/Keq) normalized by the same factor at the laboratory conversion; optimize plant per-pass conversion below equilibrium, with catalyst inventory inversely proportional to resulting net productivity and reported 10%-activity cycle life applied when available.
alternatives: Rank directly by reported rate without equilibrium correction
Fit one Temkin-Pyzhev parameter set to all catalysts
Arrhenius-extrapolate every catalyst to a common temperature and pressure
Assume plant conversion equals laboratory conversion
reason: The extracted papers rarely provide enough reaction-order and Arrhenius information for consistent global fits, whereas all usable records provide local rate, feed, conversion, temperature, and pressure. Normalized thermodynamic driving force preserves measured catalyst differences while preventing operation beyond equilibrium and exposing recycle/catalyst tradeoffs.

choice: Use an adiabatic catalytic fixed-bed synthesis converter embedded in a high-pressure recycle loop; for each literature record retain its reported catalyst temperature and pressure, and optimize per-pass N2 conversion below equilibrium against recycle compression, separation load, and catalyst inventory.
alternatives: Force every catalyst to a single industrial temperature and pressure
reason: Industrial ammonia synthesis is naturally represented by fixed beds and recycle, while the literature records are heterogeneous in feasible T/P. Retaining record conditions avoids unsupported kinetic extrapolation and optimizing conversion exposes the economic tradeoff central to the question.

choice: Cool the converter effluent, condense NH3, separate liquid product from N2/H2, purge a small gas fraction, and recycle the remaining gas with pressure-drop recompression; model residual NH3 in recycle through a pressure- and temperature-dependent recovery assumption range.
alternatives: Absorption separation integrated in the reactor
Cryogenic distillation of the full loop gas
reason: Condensation plus recycle is compatible with the broad catalyst set and makes separation/recycle duty respond to per-pass conversion; integrated absorption is only demonstrated for one paper and would bias comparison toward that specific configuration.

choice: Set the battery limit at pure N2 and H2 feeds entering at 30 bar and liquid NH3 leaving at 20 bar, including synthesis compression, reactor, heat recovery, condensation, separation, recycle, purge, storage allowance and offsites, while excluding upstream H2 generation and air separation but charging stoichiometric feed purchases.
alternatives: Start with natural gas and air
reason: The research question is catalyst choice within ammonia synthesis; upstream production technology would dominate and obscure catalyst effects. Charging delivered N2/H2 still captures feedstock attenuation of catalyst improvements.

choice: Use atomic nitrogen adsorption free energy on transition-metal sites as the descriptor; represent dissociative N2 adsorption, H2 adsorption, three sequential N-H formation steps, and NH3 desorption in a reversible single-site mean-field MKM. Apply linear adsorbate scaling and BEP barriers so strong binding favors N2 activation but penalizes hydrogenation/desorption, generating a Sabatier volcano; map TOF to catalyst productivity with a declared accessible-site density and loading basis.
alternatives: Direct polynomial fit from descriptor to plant cost without elementary steps
reason: Nitrogen binding is the established ammonia-synthesis volcano coordinate and naturally represents the central tradeoff between N2 activation and removal/hydrogenation of strongly bound N-containing intermediates. It also maps across Fe, Co, Ru, Mo, Ni, Re and Rh while permitting explicit thermodynamic reversal.
